Happy Birthday Pramukh Swami Maharaj

Never asking ‘how are things running?’, ‘Is everything okay?, ‘Is the Akshardham I built in Delhi running okay?’, ‘Is the mandir I built in London still attracting visitors?’

No, not a single question. You trusted those you had guided, nurtured, and appointed.
You did everything, but never owned anything.
You built this entire global spiritual organisation from the ground up, but were attached to only God. 

From inspecting plans and examining stones, you were now waving chadis and throwing balls. But you were still joyful.

And yes, we will forever sing songs of your glory of those glorious days when you were an active and unstoppable force walking from house to house, and leading so many projects worldwide. 

But amazingly, we will also fondly remember these years when you were bound to a wheelchair.

Because you were our Bapa. Still the same smile, the same radiance, and the same inspiration.

events.desc:
Even now, at 91, his care for the environment is lived out in the smallest of gestures. 
- He never lets the tap run when brushing his teeth, he fills a small vessel and uses only what is needed. 
- Just last month, he waited patiently for an ant to climb out of a sink before letting the water flow. 
- Earlier this year in Melbourne, a few horses were grazing outside his residence. He had been resting, but upon waking, his very first question was whether the horses had been fed and cared for. 

At 91. Imagine, then, the decades before, how many animals he must have noticed, how many trees he must have planted, how many small, unseen acts of compassion he must have carried out. 
For Mahant Swami Maharaj, to love God is to love all that God has made.

Bhagwan Swaminarayan is born as Ghanshyam in Chhapaiya.

Mother Earth celebrates the birth of Bhagwan Swaminarayan...
Darkness disappeared. The night of Rama Navami blossomed into day, aglow with hope and happiness.
On 3 April 1781 CE (Chaitra sud 9, VS 1837), at 10.10pm, Bhagwan Swaminarayan was born to Bhaktimata and Dharmadev in the small village of Chhapaiya, near Ayodhya. 

The whole village celebrated. Elders gathered with gifts, while Dharmadev Pande generously donated grains and clothes. But nothing matched the love and sparkle in the eyes of the women inside, who crowded the bedside to glimpse the face of the divine child.

On this day, during the final year of his travels as Nilkanth Varni, Bhagwan Swaminarayan graced the village of Bochasan. He stayed at the edge of the village pond. He accepted an invitation from the family of Kashidas and was sincerely served rice and yoghurt by his mother Naniba. He also performed arti of the murtis of Rama, Lakshman, and Sita at the village Ramji Mandir.

Bhagwan Swaminarayan would later visit this village many times during his travels, promising Kashidas on many occasions that a grand mandir would be established in this village in the future. 

Graced with the footprints of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, this village was later to become home to a grand shikharbaddh mandir opened 108 years later by Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj on 5 June 1907.

After his epic 2,609 days (7 years, 1 month and 23 days) of pilgrimage throughout India, covering over 12,000 kilometres, Nilkanth arrived in Loj.

Nilkanth bathed in the stepwell and retired into a meditative posture beneath a sprawling banyan tree nearby. 

Sukhanand Swami from Ramanand Swami’s ashram came to fill his pot from the stepwell.

Upon seeing the gentle, teenage yogi, he, too, was mesmerised. He came and stood before Nilkanth, waiting for him to open his eyes.

Sukhanand Swami asked: “Brahmachariji, where do you come from? What is your name? Who are your parents? Why have you renounced your home? And who is your guru?” 

 “Sadhuram! A renunciant has no caste, country or relatives. One who redeems from worldly bondage is a true parent or guru! I am in search of such a guru,” Nilkanth replied softly.

Nilkanth Varni then proceeded to the ashram in Loj to meet Muktanand Swami. Nilkanth revealed to Muktanand Swami: “My mind is at peace in your ashram. The sadhus here are of a peaceful disposition.” 

“You may ask freely whatever questions you have,” Muktanand Swami  requested.

Nilkanth then posed the five questions he had been asking throughout his travels. Muktanand Swami satisfactorily elaborated upon the natures of jiva, ishwar, maya, Brahma and Parabrahma. Nilkanth was satisfied with the answers and decided to stay at the ashram for the darshan of guru Ramanand Swami.

Nilkanth Varni writes letter to Guru Ramanand Swami.

After arriving at the village of Loj on 21 August 1799 after seven years of intense vicharan on foot, 18-year-old Nilkanth Varni yearned for the darshan of Ramanand Swami. 

When Ramanand Swami did not arrive from Kutch, Muktanand Swami told Nilkanth Varni to pen a letter which he wrote on 15 March 1800 requesting Ramanand Swami to give him darshan soon.

Well known as the 'patri' in the Swaminarayan Sampradaya, this historic letter has been poeticised by Sadguru Nishkulanand Swami in Chapter 42 of the Bhaktachintamani.

events.desc:
Following his 7-year van vicharan and 10 long months in Loj, 19-year-old Nilkanth Varni first meets Guru Ramanand Swami in the village of Piplana on 18 June 1800.

Ramanand Swami repeated what he had been saying for many years: “I am only a drumbeater, but the real actor is this brahmachari Nilkanth.”

Four months later, in Piplana, on 28 October 1800 (Kartak sud 11), he gave bhagvati diksha to Nilkanth and named him Sahajanand Swami and Narayanmuni.

Nishkulanand Swami describes this meeting in Piplana in prakran 44 of the Bhaktachintamani:
Param hitkārī bahunāmī, dīṭhā sinhāsan par swāmī. 25
Tene dekhīne pāmyā ānand, tyāre uṭhyā Swāmī Rāmānand;
Karyā Nīlkanṭhe danḍavat, tene uṭhāḍyā swāmīe tarat. 26
Preme maḷīne besāryā pās, karī bījānī bahu āsavās;
Jevā kahyātā sādhue maḷī, tevā dīṭhā chhe Varṇīe vaḷī. 27
Pāmyā paramānand sukh bhārī, āvyā harṣhanā nayaṇe vāri;
Thayā brahmachārī romānchite, joī rahyā sāmu bahu prītye. 28
Tem joī rahyā swāmī hete, ek mīṭe maṭakā rahite;

Thayā brahmachārī romānchite, joī rahyā sāmu bahu prītye. 28
Tem joī rahyā swāmī hete, ek mīṭe maṭakā rahite;

28 October 1800
Kartik sud 11
Diksha ceremony in Piplana

On 28 October 1800, Nilkanth Varni - later known as Bhagwan Swaminarayan - received diksha (spiritual initiation) in the village of Piplana, marking a pivotal moment in the Swaminarayan tradition. 

This initiation ceremony was performed by Sadguru Ramanand Swami, an eminent guru and ascetic who was widely respected. 

The event was not only the culmination of Nilkanth Varni’s years of intense spiritual journey and ascetic practices, but also the beginning of a profound new chapter in his life.

Nilkanth Varni had left home as a young boy of 11 and embarked on a seven-year journey through the forests, mountains, and towns of India, exploring various philosophies and spiritual traditions.

His quest led him to Ramanand Swami, who immediately recognized Nilkanth’s unique spiritual wisdom and divine qualities. 

After meeting in Piplana four months earlier, Ramanand Swami decided that Nilkanth Varni was ready for the path of renunciation and, thus, performed the sacred diksha ceremony. 

During this ceremony, Nilkanth Varni was given the names Sahajanand Swami and Narayan Muni, marking his entry into the holy order of sadhus under Sadguru Ramanand Swami.

Early morning, before the pre-dawn hours, Ramanand Swami arranged a ritual bath for Sahajanand Swami by the river Bhadarganga. The Brahmins chanted mantras and Ramanand Swami, Muktanand Swami and others performed the 16 rituals of worship of Sahajanand Swami. Thereafter, Sahajanand Swami put on a pair of new clothes, and after completing his daily puja rituals went with Ramanand Swami to the assembly hall. Sahajanand Swami and Ramanand Swami sat before the yagna fire and performed the rituals. Then Ramanand Swami led the twenty-one-year-old Sahajanand Swami to a decorative, high seat and officially appointed him as his successor and head of the Fellowship. The assembly hailed the name of Sahajanand Swami with thunderous applause. 

Ramanand Swami said to Sahajanand Swami: “Swami, I am very happy with you for suppressing your spirit of renunciation to accept this seat at my word. I do not know what to give to you because you are the supreme master and the all-doer. But still I feel that I should give something as a gift to you. Pray, tell me what should I offer you.” 

Sahajanand Swami prostrated in veneration to guru Ramanand Swami and humbly declared, “You are my guru. Out of love and reverence you have appointed me as the head. On this occasion I would like you to bless me with two boons.” 

“Swami, my heart shudders at the miseries of devotees. Therefore if your devotee is to suffer the pain of a scorpion bite then let that pain come to me multiplied millions of times in every pore of my body instead. And if your devotee is fated to have the begging bowl then let the begging bowl come to me instead, and may your devotee not be miserable because of food and clothes. I ask you to grant me these two boons." 

Then Ramanand Swami called Mulji Sharma of Bhadra on stage and introduced him to Sahajanand Swami. The latter responded, “Mulji is my abode, Akshardham. In future he will be initiated as a sadhu and be named as Gunatitanand Swami.”

On 17 December 1801, while meditating, Ramanand Swami passed away and went to Akshardham. Divine light emanated all around.

As news spread of Ramanand Swami’s demise, thousands of devotees became overwhelmed with grief. 

Although in mourning, Sahajanand Swami consoled everyone, “Great souls never leave this world. By obeying Swami’s commands, one will not feel that he has departed, and one will come to realise the manifest form of God.” 

Exactly 31 days had elapsed since Ramanand Swami had passed on the reins to Sahajanand Swami in Jetpur. 

From that day onwards, a new chapter was to unfold.

An aspirant named Shitaldas arrived in the village of Faneni hoping to have darshan of Ramanand Swami. On arrival, he was saddened to learn that Ramanand Swami has passed away a few days earlier on 17 December. 

He soon met Sahajanand Swami  who told him to chant a mantra. It was a new mantra to all.

On chanting the Swaminarayan mahamantra, Shitaldas attained samadhi in which he entered Akshardham, where he saw Sahajanand Swami himself as Paramatma, the supreme avatari of all avatars.
Awakening from samadhi, Shitaldas narrated his experience to all.

Revealing the glory of the mantra, Bhagwan Swaminarayan said, "This is the supreme mantra, and it represents our upasana. Whoever recites it will be freed of all miseries and will attain Akshardham."

Gradually, the glory of this mantra spread everywhere and soon, Sahajanand Swami became fondly known as Bhagwan Swaminarayan.

Today that mantra is chanted daily by countless the world over.

events.desc:
Bhagwan Swaminarayan stepped foot on the auspicious land of Gadhada for the very first time on 10 February 1805, drawn by the affection of his devotees.

Although his vicharan continued, he always returned to Gadhada, initially residing at Jiva Khachar's darbar and subsequently at the darbar of Dada Khachar, where he delivered numerous sermons, later collated in the Vachanamrut. 

Bhagwan Swaminarayan regarded Gadhada as his home, staying there for the next 25 years until his passing in 1830.

Bhagwan Swaminarayan opened the Gopinathji Mandir in 1828.

Many years later, as per his sankalp to construct a mandir on the hilltop on the banks of the River Ghela, Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj constructed a beautiful mandir made of marble, opened in 1951.

Today, the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir complex in Gadhada along with the adjacent darbar of Jiva Khachar depicts the numerous teachings and charitras of Bhagwan Swaminarayan through wonderful exhibits.

---

He was to make Gadhada his home for the next 25 years, until his passing in 1830. 

He first resided at the darbar of Jiva Khachar in the initial years, and then at the darbar of Dada Khachar, where many of the Vachanamrut discourses were delivered.

Bhagwan Swaminarayan established his sixth and final mandir in Gadhada, dedicated to Gopinathji Maharaj, adjacent to the darbar of Dada Khachar in October 1828.

As per the original sankalp of Bhagwan Swaminarayan to establish a mandir on the hilltop on the banks of the River Ghela, Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj constructed the Akshar-Purushottam Mandir on that very site which was consecrated in May 1951.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj further developed the mandir complex.

In 2020, Mahant Swami Maharaj opened the newly-restored darbar of Jiva Khachar in Gadhada.

Fast forward 100 years...

Around 1910, shortly after the opening of the mandir in Bochasan in 1907, Shastriji Maharaj – on his way to the large kund to bathe – stopped at the place where the mandir is currently situated.

Accompanied by one sadhu and Motibhai, Swamishri said to Motibhai, “Motibhai! Shriji Maharaj had stopped here and circled around on his Rojho horse at this location and declared, ‘I am today performing the groundbreaking ceremony of a large mandir here.’ Therefore, a mandir will definitely be situated here.” With these words, Swamishri proceeded to bathe.

Some time later, Swamishri took a surveyor to the southern part of the village of Sarangpur to the place where Shriji Maharaj had encircled on his Rojho horse and proclaimed that he was performing the ground-breaking ceremony for a large mandir. Swamishri put in a request for all of this sanctified land. The surveyor soon mapped out the land and marked it out with pegs.

It was at this place where Shastriji Maharaj started building a mandir in Sarangpur.

After many moments of struggle and despite the unprecedented challenges, Shastriji Maharaj performed the murti pratishtha of Sarangpur Mandir on 8 May 1916.

In Bhadra, Mulji Bhakta was busy diverting water to his sugarcane field situated by the riverbank. He was thinking about when Shriji Maharaj would instruct him to renounce this world. Then suddenly, he had a vision of Shriji Maharaj in the sky. Maharaj was wearing a yellow pitambar and a southern-style pagh. 

Maharaj said to Mulji Bhakta, “What have you come for and what are you doing? The divine light of Brahma has faded away from the world, so leave now.” 

Without a moment’s delay, Mulji left his work. He did not even go home, but headed straight to Gadhada to meet Maharaj. After that, Mulji requested Shri Hari to allow him to remain in his service. 

Mulji had detached himself completely from the world and had no interest whatsoever in material objects. In order that others may realize the spiritual state of Mulji, Shriji Maharaj tested him and said, “I will make you a sadhu, but have you burnt your house or have you kept it intact?” 

The simple-natured Mulji replied, “Maharaj, the house is as it is.” 

“Then go and burn it, and come back. I’ll make you a sadhu after that,” instructed Maharaj. 

To fulfil Maharaj’s order Mulji left immediately for Bhadra. Maharaj knew that Mulji would come back only after burning his house. So he immediately sent Bhaguji and called him back. From the spiritual viewpoint, Mulji had already burnt all ties of affection with his family, estate and relatives from his heart. But he was also prepared to destroy all the physical ties. Seeing his profound detachment, Maharaj showered praise on him.

A short while later in Dabhan on 20 January 1810, Mulji was initiated as a sadhu by Bhagwan Swaminarayan and renamed Gunatitanand Swami.

Bhagwan Swaminarayan's words have come true today.

Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami was the first spiritual successor of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the personified form of his divine abode, Akshardham.

Vedic Shastras, including the Bhagavad Gita, Brahma Sutras and the Upanishads, explain the infinite glory of Aksharbrahma. 

While on this earth, Gunatitanand Swami selflessly served Bhagwan Swaminarayan and explained Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s greatness to thousands of devotees. 

Similarly, Bhagwan Swaminarayan revealed Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami’s glory on many occasions.

Authored by Adi Acharya Shri Raghuvirji Maharaj of Vadtal and composed by Achintyanand Brahmachari, the Harililakalpataru shastra extols the supreme glory of Bhagwan Swaminarayan as Parabrahma Purushottam Narayan and Gunatitanand Swami as Aksharbrahma.

The below verse from the Harililakalpataru describes one such occasion, on this historic day in Dabhan, when Bhagwan Swaminarayan revealed Gunatitanand Swami's spiritual greatness: 

Mulji-sharmane dīkshām dadānasya prajāyate I
Bhuyān-metra samānando yato Dhāmāksharam cha me II

‘I am extremely happy to initiate Mulji Sharma. He is my divine abode, Akshardham.’ 
Harililakalpataru 7.17.49

Bhagwan Swaminarayan also prophesied on that day that this new initiate would become famed throughout the world by the name of ‘Gunatitanand’.

Gunātitānanda-rupam vishva-khyātam bhavishyati II
Harililakalpataru 7.17.54

"During the celebration of Hutashini at the home of Rathod Dhadhal in Sarangpur, Shriji Maharaj sang the Holi verse [as composed by Kabir]: ‘Sadguru khele Vasant.’ 

He then asked Muktanand Swami and Anand Swami, ‘Who is that sadguru?’ They both answered, ‘You are that sadguru.’ Maharaj replied, ‘I am Purushottam Bhagwan, whom the sadguru worships. And such a sadguru is this Gunatitanand Swami, who is Mul Akshar.’ 

With these words, he touched his [raas] stick on Gunatitanand Swami’s chest and said, ‘Jugo jug jivo evã jogi, jugo jug jivo evã jogiyã.’ So saying, Shriji Maharaj himself first proclaimed the glory of [Gunatitanand] Swami."

This Vachanamrut was first delivered 203 years ago.

On the night of Māgshar sudi 4, Samvat 1876 [21 November 1819], Shriji Mahārāj had come to the residential hall of the sādhus in Dādā Khāchar’s darbār in Gadhadā. He was dressed entirely in white clothes. At that time, an assembly of sādhus as well as devotees from various places had gathered before Him.

Read the Vachanamrut here.

Hear a nirupan by Pramukh Swami Maharaj on this Vachanamrut here.

21 November 1809
(Kartik sud Punam, Samvat 1866)
Mulji Sharma renounces Bhadra.
"Brahma tej sukay chhe. Ghar baline aviya chho?" 

In Bhadra, Mulji Bhakta was busy diverting water to his sugarcane field situated by the riverbank. He was thinking about when Shriji Maharaj would instruct him to renounce this world. Then suddenly, he had a vision of Shriji Maharaj in the sky. Maharaj was wearing a yellow pitambar and a southern-style pagh. 

Maharaj said to Mulji Bhakta, “What have you come for and what are you doing? The divine light of Brahma has faded away from the world, so leave now.” 

Without a moment’s delay, Mulji left his work. He did not even go home, but headed straight to Gadhada to meet Maharaj. After that, Mulji requested Shri Hari to allow him to remain in his service. 

Mulji had detached himself completely from the world and had no interest whatsoever in material objects. In order that others may realize the spiritual state of Mulji, Shriji Maharaj tested him and said, “I will make you a sadhu, but have you burnt your house or have you kept it intact?” 

The simple-natured Mulji replied, “Maharaj, the house is as it is.” 

“Then go and burn it, and come back. I’ll make you a sadhu after that,” instructed Maharaj. 

To fulfil Maharaj’s order, Mulji left immediately for Bhadra. Maharaj knew that Mulji would come back only after burning his house. So he immediately sent Bhaguji and called him back. From the spiritual viewpoint, Mulji had already burnt all ties of affection with his family, estate and relatives from his heart. But he was also prepared to destroy all the physical ties. Seeing his profound detachment, Maharaj showered praise on him.

A short while later in Dabhan on 20 January 1810, Mulji was ordained as a sadhu by Bhagwan Swaminarayan and renamed Gunatitanand Swami.

In 1821, Bhagwan Swaminarayan was in the village of Panchala, Gujarat, to celebrate the Holi festival. 

He gave the sadhus a small piece of sandalwood each. The followingmorning, Bhagwan Swaminarayan did not see a tilak on any sadhus' foreheads. After further inquiry, he found that the sadhus had consumed the sandalwood, thinking it to be prasad. He distributed another piece and instructed them to perform a tilak.

The next day, he saw that the sadhus had applied tilaks of different shapes and sizes.

Bhagwan Swaminarayan then requested Gunatitanand Swami to come forward. With his own hands, Bhagwan Swaminarayan applied a sandalwood tilak and a round chandlo of kumkum on the forehead of Gunatitanand Swami.

Showing the tilak-chandlo to all, Bhagwan Swaminarayan stated, “This is our tilak. No God can compare with me and no sadhu can compare with this sadhu [Gunatitanand Swami].” 

In this manner, Maharaj conveyed to others his own matchless identity as Purushottam and the identity of Gunatitanand Swami as his personified abode Aksharbrahma.

In Vachanamrut Gadhada II 27, Bhagwan Swaminarayan explains that he established mandirs for the preservation of upasana and devotion to God.

In his lifetime, Bhagwan Swaminarayan constructed six mandirs between 1822 and 1828.
1. Ahmedabad (1822)
2. Bhuj (1823)
3. Vadtal (1824)
4. Dholera (1826)
5. Junagadh (1828)
6. Gadhada (1828)

The first of these mandirs was opened in Kalupur in Ahmedabad on 24 February 1822, built on land gifted by the British rulers of that time.

---

Mahant Swami Maharaj has also mentioned Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s reason for constructing mandirs in Satsang Diksha:

Shuddhopāsana-bhaktim hi
poshayitum cha rakshitum; 
Bhakti mandira-nirmāṇa-
rūpām prāvartayaddharahi. 87

Tathaivā’gnāpāyam āsa
sevārtham Harinā saha;
Tasya chottama-bhaktasya 
tasyevaivā’kshrasya cha. 88

Shri Harie shuddha upāsanā-bhaktinā poshan ane rakshan māte mandir nirmān-rup bhaktinu pravartan karyu. Ane Bhagwanni jemaj temnā uttam bhakta evā Aksharbrahmani Bhagwanni sāthe sevā karvā māte āgnā kari. (87-88)

Shri Hari inspired the creation of mandirs as a form of devotion to foster and protect pure upāsanā and bhakti. He instructed that, along with Bhagwan, one should also serve his supreme devotee, Aksharbrahma, in the very same manner that one serves Bhagwan. (87-88)

The then Lord Bishop of Calcutta, Bishop Heber met Bhagwan Swaminarayan.

This meeting is considered to be a significant event in the history of the Swaminarayan Sampraday.

During their meeting, Bhagwan Swaminarayan explained his philosophy and teachings to Bishop Heber, and the two had a fruitful discussion. Bishop Heber was impressed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan's ideas and the devotion of his followers. See above some quotes from Bishop Heber's Journal.

The meeting between Bishop Heber and Bhagwan Swaminarayan is remembered as a significant moment in the history of interfaith dialogue in India, as it brought together two leaders from different religions in a respectful and productive conversation.

179 years later in 2004, His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj opened a 'Smruti Mandir' in the city of Nadiad as a permanent memory of this historic meeting.

To learn more about Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the British, watch this video https://youtu.be/wVfDGO_YmKw

Bhagatji Maharaj shone as a radiant beacon of unwavering devotion, illuminating the path of spirituality for countless souls. Selected discourses of Bhagwan Swaminarayan given between 1819 and 1829 have been compiled in the Vachanamrut which contains a total of 273 discourses.

Narrated on 25 July 1829, the last recorded Vachanamrut was  'Gadhada III-39: Vishalyakaraṇī Aushadhinu'.

In the conclusion of this final Vachanamrut, Bhagwan Swaminarayan says:
▪️"It is the principle of all of the scriptures that one should eradicate māyā and develop love for God."
▪️ “A devotee of God requires the strength of two things: ātmā-realization and the greatness of God."
▪️"I deliver these discourses to you not from any imagination of my mind, nor to display any sort of aptitude. I have experienced all that I have spoken about. In fact, I speak in accordance to what I practice."

It was also the final Vachanamrut that was read to Yogiji Maharaj. On the early morning of 16 January 1971, a week before he passed away to Akshardham, Yogiji Maharaj asked for the Vachanamrut to be read. The sevak read this Vachanamut. After this, until his passing, Yogiji Maharaj was not able to listen to the Vachanamrut again. 

📖 Read the full Vachanamrut here.

📹 Watch a 4-part nirupan by Mahant Swami Maharaj here: https://youtu.be/g8d0b4I2OxY

Dungar was blessed by Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami when he was 15 months old.

True to those blessings, Dungar was later initiated as a sadhu and named Yagnapurushdas, popularly known as Shastriji Maharaj, who went on to propagate the Akshar-Purushottam upasana as propounded by Bhagwan Swaminarayan, constructing 5 glorious mandirs for the cause of upasana.

Following Yogiji Maharaj's sad passing on 23 January 1971, he was succeeded by Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

Following in the footsteps of his guru, Swamishri conducted his first diksha ceremony on 31 January 1971 on the auspicious day of Vasant Panchmi in Gondal.

Many parshads received bhagwati diksha in Gondal. The group of initiates included those who had accompanied Yogiji Maharaj from Africa and England, including Kamleshbhai of London, who had earlier received parshadi diksha from Yogiji Maharaj on 14 October 1970.

He became the first youth from London to be initiated as a Swaminarayan sadhu; he was renamed Sadhu Aksharviharidas.

Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami passed away to Akshardham in Gondal on 11 October 1867.

Following the agnisanskar rites on the banks of the River Gondali, his sacred ashes (asthi) were collected in a copper urn. Work soon started to construct a chhatri at the sacred site. This chhatri was completed in two months and was inaugurated on the auspicious day of Vasant Panchmi.

Known as the 'Akshar Deri', this chhatri marked the samadhi sthan of Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami.

The holy charanarvind of Bhagwan Swaminarayan were consecrated at this site followed by the pictorial murtis of Akshar-Purushottam. This shrine soon became a place of pilgrimage, fulfilling the wishes of countless devotees.

In 1934, Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj opened 'Akshar Mandir' built over the sacred Akshar Deri. This has now become a popular place of pilgrimage, frequented by devotees all over the world.

Known as the 'Akshar Deri', this chhatri marked the samadhi sthan of Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami.

The holy charanarvind of Bhagwan Swaminarayan were subsequently consecrated at this site followed by the pictorial murtis of Akshar-Purushottam. This shrine soon became a place of pilgrimage, fulfilling the wishes of countless devotees.

In 1934, Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj opened 'Akshar Mandir' built over the sacred Akshar Deri. This has now become a popular place of pilgrimage, frequented by devotees all over the world.

Acharya Viharilalji Maharaj initiates Dungar Bhagat into the sadhu order and names him ’Yagnapurushdasji’.

After renouncing his home in Mahelav in December 1881, young Dungar Bhagat remained in the association of his guru, Sadguru Vignananand Swami, as a parshad. 

When the time to ordain him as a sadhu came, a special yagna was organised in Vartal in November 1882, where he was given bhagavati diksha and renamed Sadhu Yagnapurushdas.

A few months later in Surat in March 1883, he had his first darshan of Pragji Bhakta (Bhagatji Maharaj) of Mahuva. It was from Pragji Bhakta that he was inspired to propagate the principles of Akshar-Purushottam Darshan as propounded by Bhagwan Swaminarayan.

Bhagatji Maharaj welcomed with a grand reception at Junagadh

Since his exile from the Satsang - imposed by the authorities in Vadtal for propagating the glory of Gunatitanand Swami - Bhagatji Maharaj had not visited Junagadh. 

Over 30 years had passed, yet Bhagatji Maharaj did not go to Junagadh due to opposition and the absence of Acharya Maharaj’s orders. Shastri Yagnapurushdasji, however, decided to accord a grand reception to Bhagatji at the very place where he had been insulted.

In VS 1953 (1897 CE), he persuaded Acharya Viharilalji Maharaj to invite Bhagatji on the occasion of the Janmashtami festival to be celebrated in Junagadh.

Bhagatji Maharaj arrived in Junagadh two days prior to the festival. He was received along with Acharya Maharaj at Junagadh railway station with all the traditional pomp. Like Acharya Maharaj, Bhagatji Maharaj and his followers were driven in a decorated carriage. Special arrangements were made at the mandir to make their stay comfortable. Yagnapurushdasji was assisted by Kothari Jibhai of Junagadh in making these arrangements for Bhagatji.

The news of Bhagatji’s arrival in Junagadh spread all over the city. All the Nagar devotees came to the mandir for Bhagatji’s darshan. Here, he met senior sadhus such as Balmukunddasji and Jaga Bhagat, who had sincerely served Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami. For many days, these great stalwarts of the Gunatit Gnan came together to engage in discourses and scriptural discussions to extol the glory of Akshar and Purushottam.

Bhagatji's devotees had sponsored the meals on the day after Janmashtami at Junagadh Mandir where he served the sadhus and devotees most affectionately.

At the age of 68, Brahmaswarup Bhagatji Maharaj passed away to Akshardham in Mahuva after a lifetime dedicated to seva, bhakti and propagating the glory of Akshar-Purushottam as propounded by Bhagwan Swaminarayan.

Just three months earlier in August 1897, through the efforts of Shastri Yagnapurushdas (Shastriji Maharaj), Bhagatji Maharaj was welcomed in a grand way in Junagadh for the festival of Janmashtami, following which Bhagatji Maharaj and Jaga Bhagat explained the glory of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Gunatitanand Swami as well as reminisced sweet memories of their samagam of Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami in Junagadh. 

Following this,  Bhagatji Maharaj went to Gondal, where Bhagatji Maharaj and Shastri Yagnapurushdas (Shastriji Maharaj) met for the final time and parted at the Akshar Deri, where Bhagatji revealed that a grand mandir would later be built over the Akshar Deri.

Yogiji Maharaj in his historic and heartfelt prarthana on 9 December 1966 in Mahelav said: "When Bhagatji left his body, Swami [Shastriji Maharaj] received the sad news in Rajkot. Ramji Bhatt was sitting with him at the time. He remarked, 'The earth's auspiciousness has now gone, for Bhagatji was auspiciousness on this earth.' 

"It was then that Shastriji Maharaj revealed, 'Satpurush kadi pruthvi uparthi jatā ja nathi: the Satpurush never leaves the earth.'"

Bhagataji‌-Maha‌ra‌ja- sa‌ksha‌d-vigna‌na-mu‌rtaye...
Bhagatji Maharaj: the embodiment of wisdom

9 February 1905 
Maha sud 5, VS 1961
Vadhwan, India

On the auspicious day of Vasant Panchmi in 1905, the stone murtis of Akshar-Purushottam were consecrated for the first time ever in a shikharbaddh mandir, newly constructed in Vadhwan with the support of Shastriji Maharaj.

After leaving Vartal a few months later, Shastriji Maharaj would go on to build and inaugurate five shikharbaddh mandirs dedicated to Akshar-Purushottam over the next 45 years.

While discussions about the Akshar-Purushottam philosophy did take place in some nooks and corners of Vartal and other mandirs of the Swaminarayan Sampraday, it was a knowledge not always easy to digest, despite its prevalence from the time of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. 

In April 1905, the Chaitra Punam festival would soon be celebrated in Vartal. Shastriji Maharaj was ill in Chansad at the time.

With Swamishri’s consent, Kalidasbhai and Galbhai of Chansad and several other devotees set out for Vartal to attend the festival.

As soon as Acharya Maharaj arrived in the Punam assembly, Galbhai exclaimed, “Sahajanand Swami Maharajni Jay!” Everyone repeated the call. 

Immediately Galbhai followed, “Akshar-Purushottam Maharajni Jay!” 
Again, everyone repeated.

This was maybe the first time that this jay was extolled publicly at such a gathering.

Today, due to the efforts of the Gunatit Gurus, that same jaynaad glorifying Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj is hailed at hundreds of mandirs and thousands of homes around the world.

19 April 1981 
Chaitra sud Punam

Inauguration of Yagnapurush Smruti Mandir, Sarangpur, by Pramukh Swami Maharaj

Exactly a week after celebrating the 200th birth anniversary of his isthadev, Parabrahma Purushottam Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan, Pramukh Swami Maharaj opened a mandir built over the samadhi sthan of his guru, Shastriji Maharaj.

It had been a struggle to complete the mandir, but Swamishri had ensured its completion through personally managing the project, which paid homage to the tremendous efforts of Shastriji Maharaj in propagating the eternal upasana of Akshar-Purushottam.

This Yagnapurush Smruti Mandir has been a witness to Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s guru-bhakti. Many have done darshan of his overflowing joy at doing darshan of his guru. Even when ill and frail in Sarangpur, he would regularly insist on going for darshan at the mandir.

Even on 17 August 2016, after he had reverted to Akshardham four days earlier, his divine body was taken to the smruti mandir for one last time.

Swamishri’s guru-bhakti was such that he had instructed years before that his final rites be performed at a location directly opposite this mandir so that Shastriji Maharaj’s drashti would remain upon him for eternity.

It was a sad day in many ways, but significant and life-changing nevertheless. 

Having received initiation as a sadhu at the age of 17 in November 1882, Shastriji Maharaj had spent almost 23 years in Vartal as a sadhu where his unmatched saintliness and penetrating discourses inspired many. 

He wished to continue to preach the principle of Akshar-Purushottam as laid down by Bhagwan Swaminarayan in Vachanamruts such as Gadhada I 71 and Gadhada II 21.

Much opposition came his way, but he merely tolerated and continued his mission in the footsteps of his guru Bhagatji Maharaj.

After much consideration and the guidance of seniors such as Krishnaji Ada, it was on this morning that Shastri Yagnapurushdas offered prayers in front of the sacred murti of Harikrishna Maharaj in Vartal to take leave as he embarked on his mission to propound the Vedic principle of Akshar-Purushottam as established by Bhagwan Swaminarayan. 

On that first day, there were 5 sadhus and a handful of haribhaktas. 

Despite the overwhelming odds and insurmountable challenges, through his sheer determination, unparalleled dedication and deep faith, he would go on to establish Akshar-Purushottam mandirs in Bochasan, Sarangpur, Gondal, Atladra and Gadhada over the following 45 years.

Evā Shastriji Maharajne amārā lākho vandan ho...

1 November 1908 (Kartik sud 7) Dhari, Gujarat

A devout child from his early years, Jhinabhai of Dhari departed from home on 1 November 1908 for Junagadh. 

Born to parents Puribai and Devchandbhai in 1892, this bal-bhakta was engrossed in devotion from a young age. From studies to meditation to seva to samagam, he excelled in every aspect.

The frequent visits from the sadhus based at the Swaminarayan Mandir in Junagadh helped foster his devotional service and through their association, he had no longing for anything else than to renounce and become a sadhu.

At the Swaminarayan Mandir in Junagadh consecrated by Bhagwan Swaminarayan and where Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami had stayed for 40 years, Jhinabhai was given parshadi diksha by his guru, Krishnacharandas Swami a week later on 8 November 1908. He was given the name of Jhina Bhagat.

A devout child from his early years, Jhinabhai of Dhari departed from home on 1 November 1908 for Junagadh. At the Swaminarayan Mandir consecrated by Bhagwan Swaminarayan and where Aksharbrahma  Gunatitanand had stayed for 40 years, Jhinabhai was given parshadi diksha by his guru Krishnacharandas Swami. He was then given the name Jhina Bhagat. 

In the future, this same Jhina Bhagat would be known around the world as Yogiji Maharaj, and would go on to give diksha to 51 educated youths and thereby mark a new era in India's rich sadhu parampara.

Jina Bhagat (Yogiji Maharaj) met Shastriji Maharaj for the first time.

In August 1909, Shastriji Maharaj arrived in Rajkot where he stayed at the house of Krishnaji Ada. 

Some sadhus and parshads from Junagadh were also in vicharan in Rajkot at the time. When Jina Bhagat of Junagadh heard this news of Shastriji Maharaj, he felt a strong desire to have the darshan of Shastriji Maharaj, as he had often heard of the glory of Shastriji Maharaj from various sadhus and devotees in Junagadh.

So, early in the morning, under the pretext of going for a bath in the Aji river, Jina Bhagat and three other sadhus proceeded to the house of Krishnaji Ada.

When Shastriji Maharaj awoke, Jadavjibhai informed him that some sadhus had come for darshan. Shastriji Maharaj went to the room where the sadhus were waiting. 

Jina Bhagat and the other sadhus paid reverence to Shastriji Maharaj before presenting to him a sactified mala and tumbdi, which had been used by Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami. Shastriji Maharaj was greatly pleased.

Jina Bhagat could not take his eyes off Shastriji Maharaj and looked at him with great reverence. Shastriji Maharaj, too, looked at Jina Bhagat with much affection.

From that day, Jina Bhagat mentally accepted Shastriji Maharaj as his guru.

Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj was born as Jhinabhai in the village of Dhari on 23 May 1892. 

His childhood was one of devotion par excellence along with samagam of the visiting sadhus from the Swaminarayan Mandir in Junagadh, including Sadguru Krishnacharan Swami.

It was under the guidance of Krishnacharan Swami that young Jhinabhai renounced home at the tender age of 16 with the blessings of his family. He joined the order of parshads in Junagadh in November 1908.

In Junagadh, young Jhina Bhagat served in various capacities as a parshad, winning the affection of the sadhus and devotees.

On the morning of 11 April 1911, 18-year-old Jhina Bhagat took bhagvati diksha into saffron at the hands of Acharya Shripatiprasadji Maharaj in Vartal.

On this auspicious occasion, Jhina Bhagat was renamed Sadhu Gnanjivandasji.

Due to his austere and devout nature, the sadhus and devotees fondly called him ‘Yogi’ or 'Jogi' while Krishnacharandas Swami called him ‘Gnanji Swami’.

He served as a sadhu in Junagadh Mandir for three months before taking a decision that turned out to be a pivotal development in the history of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha.

---

On this auspicious occasion, Jhina Bhagat was renamed Sadhu Gnanjivandasji.

Due to his austere and devout nature, the sadhus and devotees fondly called him ‘Yogi’ or 'Jogi' while Krishnacharandas Swami called him ‘Gnanji Swami’.

He served as a sadhu in Junagadh Mandir for three months before taking a decision that turned out to be a pivotal development in the history of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha.

Before the sun rose on that early July morning in Junagadh, Yogiji Maharaj and a group of 7 sadhus departed from the Swaminarayan Mandir in Junagadh to join Shastriji Maharaj in his noble mission of propagating the Akshar-Purushottam upasana.

Having received bhagvati diksha barely 3 months previously on 11 April 1911 when he was named Gnanjivandas Swami, 19-year-old Yogiji Maharaj was accompanied by the small sacred murti of Harikrishna Maharaj. This murti had been sanctified by Bhagwan Swaminarayan and daily worshipped by Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami.  

Since that day, the murti has been reverently worshipped by the gurus of the Aksharbrahmaswarup Gunatit Guru Parampara.

---

9 JULY 1911 (Ashadh sud 13)
Junagadh

Before the sun rose on that early July morning in Junagadh, Yogiji Maharaj and a group of 7 sadhus departed from the Swaminarayan Mandir in Junagadh to join Shastriji Maharaj in his noble mission of propagating the Akshar-Purushottam upasana.

Having received bhagvati diksha barely 3 months previously on 11 April 1911 when he was named Gnanjivandas Swami, 19-year-old Yogiji Maharaj was accompanied by the small sacred murti of Harikrishna Maharaj. This murti had been sanctified by Bhagwan Swaminarayan and daily worshipped by Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami.  

Since that day, the murti has been reverently worshipped by the gurus of the Aksharbrahmaswarup Gunatit Guru Parampara.

Following the opening of the first BAPS shikharbaddha mandir dedicated to Akshar-Purushottam upasana in Bochasan (1907), Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj opened the second such mandir in Sarangpur.

This land had been sanctified by Bhagwan Swaminarayan a hundred years previously when he rode the Rojho Godo and declared his wish to build a grand mandir.

The history of BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Sarangpur, is an extraordinary story of human commitment and divine grace. The mandir land and the village of Sarangpur had the privilege of being blessed by the visits and prayers of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Gunatitanand Swami, the 500 paramhansas and Bhagatji Maharaj. Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj put in immense efforts into the construction of this mandir, despite the numerous challenges, intense opposition and overwhelming odds.

---

8 May 2016
Sarangpur, India

During the Sarangpur Mandir Shatabdi Mahotsav, Pramukh Swami Maharaj gave a ‘kol’ to take all to Akshardham. This was to be the final time he gave such an ‘Akshardhamno kol’. 

All were witness to his unparalleled ishta-bhakti on this occasion as well. In every moment of his life, he put God forward. Age, circumstances, the scale of his achievements over all these decades, even the condition of his own body could massively change, but nothing could sway him from his ishta-bhakti. That remained unchanging, because that is who he was, at his core. The same ishta-bhakti he had throughout his life, was the same ishta-bhakti he had in the final year of his life, when his hands could barely move, but he'd still always reach out for his beloved Thakorji, because that devotion to God was never something he learnt or cultivated; it was who he was.

For many around the world, this ‘Akshardhamno kol’ is etched in our hearts as a permanent reminder of the everlasting peace that the Satpurush can grant. Despite the many challenges, hardships, and miseries life can bring, in such moments, the Satpurush can grant us with bliss. Such reassurances fill hearts with joy and security and make so many fearless in the face of death, disease, disappointment, and despair.

Shantilal leaves home to become a sadhu. He is given parshadi diksha and then bhagvati diksha by Shastriji Maharaj. A short letter from guru Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj is all it took for him to let go of his life. Today, the world knows him as Pramukh Swami Maharaj. It is a day we reflect on his tyag.

Tyaga is renunciation: letting go of those things that hinder one’s quest for moksha. The Upanishads explain the importance of tyaga: “One who wants to attain God must let
go of all worldly attachments.”. The ultimate form of tyaga is not just letting go, but also selflessly sacrificing one’s self for the benefit of mankind. He left his home, his relatives, his ambitions and those dear to him to selflessly give his all for God, guru, and humanity. Until his very last breath, Swamishri lived by the sentiments with which he renounced: devotion and selfless service. The Kaivalya Upanishad states, “Immortality cannot be achieved by wealth, power or good deeds. It can only be achieved by tyag.” Pramukh Swami Maharaj is immortal.

Hearing Shanti Bhagat's reply of "no," Shastriji Maharaj said, "I want to arrange for you to have darshan of Sarangpur. Come with me."

When Shanti Bhagat asked Shastriji Maharaj if he should inform Hariswarupdas, Shastriji Maharaj replied, "What's the need in asking him? You come." However, thinking it would be better to ask since he was staying with Hariswarupdas, Shanti Bhagat approached him and informed him of his plans. Hariswarupdas became angry and threatened, "If you go, I will not let you come back to Bhadran. You are not to go." Shanti Bhagat, shocked by this response, approached Shastriji Maharaj for a solution. Shastriji Maharaj spoke to Hariswarupdas, saying, "This bhagat is still new and wants to visit Sarangpur, so let him go." Thus, Shastriji Maharaj personally took Shanti Bhagat to Sarangpur.

On Tuesday 2 January 1940, Shanti Bhagat arrived in Sarangpur for the first time. The blessed land was delighted to welcome the one who was to later make this his eternal home.

Shanti Bhagat was overjoyed to see the beautiful, sky-touching mandir of Sarangpur. Seeing this masterpiece created by Shastriji Maharaj, he realised his glory even further. Shastriji Maharaj explained to Shanti Bhagat the greatness of this place and the murtis in the mandir.

Ever since that day, Sarangpur held a special place in the mind of Shanti Bhagat. Such was the good fortune of Sarangpur!

A few days later, Shastriji Maharaj took Shanti Bhagat to Gondal, where the young parshads was overjoyed to have darshan of Akshar Mandir for the first time.

It was at the sacred Akshar Deri there that he would be given bhagvati diksha by Shastriji Maharaj on the morning of 10 January 1940.

---

2 January 1940
Sarangpur, India

On this day, Shanti Bhagat (later known as Pramukh Swami Maharaj) stepped foot on the sanctified soil of Sarangpur for the first time ever.

After studying for a month in Bhadran, the student sadhus were called to Ahmedabad to attend the parayan organised during the month of Magshar in December 1939 CE. Following the parayan, Shastriji Maharaj asked Shanti Bhagat: "Have you had darshan of Sarangpur Mandir?"
Hearing Shanti Bhagat's reply of "no," Shastriji Maharaj said, "I want to arrange for you to have darshan of Sarangpur. Come with me."

When Shanti Bhagat asked Shastriji Maharaj if he should inform Hariswarupdas, Shastriji Maharaj replied, "What's the need in asking him? You come." However, thinking it would be better to ask since he was staying with Hariswarupdas, Shanti Bhagat approached him and informed him of his plans. Hariswarupdas became angry and threatened, "If you go, I will not let you come back to Bhadran. You are not to go." Shanti Bhagat, shocked by this response, approached Shastriji Maharaj for a solution. Shastriji Maharaj spoke to Hariswarupdas, saying, "This bhagat is still new and wants to visit Sarangpur, so let him go." Thus, Shastriji Maharaj personally took Shanti Bhagat to Sarangpur.

On Tuesday 2 January 1940, Shanti Bhagat arrived in Sarangpur for the first time. The blessed land was delighted to welcome the one who was to later make this his eternal home.

Shanti Bhagat was overjoyed to see the beautiful, sky-touching mandir of Sarangpur. Seeing this masterpiece created by Shastriji Maharaj, he realised his glory even further. Shastriji Maharaj explained to Shanti Bhagat the greatness of this place and the murtis in the mandir.

Ever since that day, Sarangpur held a special place in the mind of Shanti Bhagat. Such was the good fortune of Sarangpur!

A few days later, Shastriji Maharaj took Shanti Bhagat to Gondal, where the young parshads was overjoyed to have darshan of Akshar Mandir for the first time.

It was at the sacred Akshar Deri there that he would be given bhagvati diksha by Shastriji Maharaj on the morning of 10 January 1940.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj Bhagvati Diksha

On the morning of Wednesday 10 January 1940, after Yogiji Maharaj performed the mahapuja at the sacred Akshar Deri in Gondal, Shastriji Maharaj performed the initiation rites and decided that Shanti Bhagat be named Narayanswarupdas, explaining, “He is the very form of Narayan.”

He then told Yogiji Maharaj to bless Narayanswarup Swami, so that he acquire virtues like his.

Yogiji Maharaj completes writing the ‘Sunrut’ letter contained in the Yogi Gita. This was a letter written by Yogiji Maharaj to a devotee of Ahmedabad. He began writing the letter on 28 March 1941 and completed it on this day. This letter has become a timeless source of profound spiritual wisdom.

Yogiji Maharaj mentions 7 important points in this letter:
1. Service, Humility and Attaining God’s Abode 
2. Avoid Gossip 
3. See One’s Faults 
4. Tolerance, Forgiveness
5. Mutual Affection 
6. Virtues of Assistance, Service and Tolerance
7. Spiritual Discourses

These were the first murtis to be officially consecrated in a Swaminarayan mandir outside of India.

The devotees of East Africa had been gathering for satsang assemblies under the guidance of Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj, Nirgundas Swami, and other senior swamis. These regular gatherings resulted in the consecration of these murtis.

---

26 December 1945
Nairobi, Kenya

On 26 December 1945, painted murtis of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami and Aksharmukta Gopalanand Swami, which had been sanctified by Shastriji Maharaj in Anand in August 1945, were installed with great festivity in Nairobi by Shri Harmanbhai at the Swaminarayan Mandir on Temple Street.

These were the first murtis to be officially consecrated in a Swaminarayan mandir outside of India.

The devotees of East Africa had been gathering for satsang assemblies under the guidance of Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj, Nirgundas Swami, and other senior swamis. These regular gatherings resulted in the consecration of these murtis.

These murtis are still preserved today.

events.desc:
Sadguru Nirgundas Swami passes away to Akshardham

Nirgundas Swami was a pioneer in the history of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha. He surrendered his genius, personality and standing at the feet of Shastriji Maharaj, who he humbly served until his last breath. 

In a letter dated  28 July 1949 to the politician Gulzarilal Nanda, Nirgundas Swami proclaims, “Shastriji Maharaj was never influenced by anyone and was able to control such free-willed people as me.” 

Moreover, he wrote in his personal journal: “No one had the courage to tell me to wear saffron [to become a sadhu], but Shastriji Maharaj did. He told me that my intellect, knowledge, and ability would shine more in saffron than in white. These words touched me and I became a sadhu.”

Such was Nirgundas Swami’s respect for Shastriji Maharaj, he would carry out any command given by his guru to earn his rajipo.

Inspired by Gunatitanand Swami’s vision of Satsang being spread to all corners of the Earth and by Shastriji Maharaj’s words, Nirgundas Swami began writing of the greatness of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj and Shastriji Maharaj in a stream of letters to Africa, where Harmanbhai and Maganbhai, two devotees, had established Satsang. Nirgundas Swami’s letters were not just a few pages long, but were sometimes up to a hundred pages in length! Moreover, his letters were organised, well-written, point-to-point, clear, and faithful to the principles of the Vachanamrut and other scriptures of the Sampraday.

Shastriji Maharaj would often speak of the pivotal role played by Nirgundas Swami in propagating the Akshar-Purushottam upasana through vicharan, letters and katha.

---

30 May 1950
Anand, Gujarat, India

Sadguru Nirgundas Swami passes away to Akshardham

Such was Nirgundas Swami’s respect for Shastriji Maharaj, he would carry out any command given by his guru to earn his rajipo.

Inspired by Gunatitanand Swami’s vision of Satsang being spread to all corners of the Earth and by Shastriji Maharaj’s words, Nirgundas Swami began writing of the greatness of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj and Shastriji Maharaj in a stream of letters to Africa, where Harmanbhai and Maganbhai, two devotees, had established Satsang. Nirgundas Swami’s letters were not just a few pages long, but were sometimes up to a hundred pages in length! Moreover, his letters were organised, well-written, point-to-point, clear, and faithful to the principles of the Vachanamrut and other scriptures of the Sampraday.

Shastriji Maharaj would often speak of the pivotal role played by Nirgundas Swami in propagating the Akshar-Purushottam upasana through vicharan, letters and katha.

To expound the pure principles of Akshar-Purushottam upasana as established by Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj created five shikharbaddha mandirs: Bochasan, Sarangpur, Gondal, Atladra and Gadhada.

On the auspicious land of Gadhada which had been blessed with the 25-year stay of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Shastriji Maharaj sought to acquire the land on the hill top on the banks of the sacred River Ghela. 

It was a colossal task, deemed impossible by many. Yet with faith in God and Guru, he persisted for 33 long years before finally acquiring the land in 1949.

Despite his advanced age and frail health, he meticulously oversaw the project of building a marble shikharbaddha mandir in Gadhada. 

During his final days in Sarangpur, despite being bedridden, he expressed a wish to travel to Gadhada. 

He travelled by car and reached Gadhada on the evening of 11 April 1951.

On the morning of 12 April 1951, he personally conducted the consecration of the murtis of Dham, Dhami and Mukta, bathing the murtis with sacred water from the River Ghela along with other pratishtha rituals.
After performing the arti, before preparing to return to Sarangpur, he exclaimed, "My vidhi is now over. Jogi Maharaj will come and complete the final consecration arti."

10 May 2016
Sarangpur, India

Last diksha given by Pramukh Swami Maharaj, as part of Sarangpur Mandir Shatabdi Utsav

After a lifetime of inspiring hundreds of youths on the path of tyagashram and many joyous, divine diksha mahotsavs, this would be the final time that Swamishri gave tyagi diksha.

From 1971 to 2016, Pramukh Swami Maharaj ordained more than 1000 youths as sadhus. To inspire this many individuals from around the world, at the prime of their life, to give up their personal ambitions, to overcome worldly desires, and to dedicate their entire lives to serving society, guru and God is nothing short of a miracle. A miracle stemming from the selfless love, purity, deep spirituality, and godliness of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. 

Alongside inspiring such youths, countless parents were inspired to happily permit their children to become sadhus. Witness the moving story of one such couple whose son took diksha on that very day: https://youtu.be/Y1WjiRIeTA4?t=3190.

In the town of Gadhpur sanctified by Bhagwan Swaminarayan from 1805 to 1830, Shastriji Maharaj went to great efforts to fulfil Bhagwan Swaminarayan's sankalp of building a grand shikharbaddh mandir on the hillock on the banks of the River Ghela.

After 33 years of perseverance in trying to acquire the land, he eventually succeeded and performed the foundation stone laying ceremony in 1949. He began the construction of a marble mandir and shortly before the scheduled pratishtha, he visited Gadhada despite being bedridden with illness in Sarangpur. 

On 12 April 1951, he bathed the murtis with water from the sacred River Ghela and performed the pratishtha rituals, before proclaiming: "My vidhi is now over. Jogi will come and perform the [final pratishtha] arti."

Six days following the passing of Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj performed the murti pratishtha of the murtis of Dham, Dhami and Mukta in the central shrine of the grand marble mandir on 16 May 1951.

It was not long after Shastriji Maharaj's passing in Sarangpur on 10 May 1951.

Six days later, Yogiji Maharaj completed the murti-pratishtha in Gadhada. 

On 19 May, rituals to mark the 17th Patotsav of Gondal Mandir were held in the presence of numerous devotees from East Africa.

After celebrating Vaishakhi Punam in Gondal, Yogiji Maharaj travelled to the region of Charotar, where he visited many villages and graced the village homes of many of those devotees who had now settled in East Africa. 

It was during this time that Yogiji Maharaj stayed for six days in Anand and visited the home of Manilal Naranbhai Patel, whose young son came in touch with Yogiji Maharaj for the very first time.

It was a life-changing spiritual experience for the 17-year-old Vinubhai. Soon after this, he was so moved by the saintliness of Yogiji Maharaj, that he longed to spend every spare moment in his guru's company.

From 1951 to 1957, young Vinubhai often rushed to Yogiji Maharaj  during his vacations. He was totally won over by Yogiji Maharaj’s selfless love, and he was determined to offer his all at the feet of Yogiji Maharaj.

This eventually culminated in Yogiji Maharaj initiating Vinubhai as a parshad in February 1957.

24 June 1990
London, UK

Pramukh Swami Maharaj decides the land on which to build the first shikkharbaddh mandir in the western world.

A short distance away and a short while previously, he had already conducted the khatmuhrat vidhi at Neasden High School.

However, amidst the dust and heat of Neasden on that summer's day, Pramukh Swami Maharaj's inner eyes spotted the potential of another site before him.

We noticed a simple 'For Sale' sign at the Arlington warehouse.

He saw a grand shikkharbaddh mandir that would be worthy of the home of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj in Great Britain.

Maha sud 2, VS 2013
Gondal, India

On this day, Vinubhai of Anand was initiated as a parshad (in white clothes) by Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj at the sacred Akshar Deri in Gondal.

Born in 1933 in Jabalpur, Vinubhai had spent much time travelling with Yogiji Maharaj from 1951 to 1957. Following the completion of his higher studies in Agriculture in 1956, he remained full time with Yogiji Maharaj. 

On his ordination in 1957, he was renamed Vinu Bhagat. 

As part of the group of 9 yogeshwars, he was again ordained as a parshad by Yogiji Maharaj in July 1960 in Mumbai.

He was later to receive bhagvati diksha at the hands of Yogiji Maharaj in 1961 and renamed Keshavjivandas Swami, later to become popularly known as Mahant Swami.

On the passing in 2016 Pramukh Swami Maharaj was succeeded by Mahant Swami Maharaj as guru of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, the sixth spiritual successor of Bhagwan Swaminarayan.

Today we celebrate that historic day of 1957 as Swamishri enters his 70th year as a tyagi.

Yogiji Maharaj departed from Mumbai for Nairobi for his second vicharan abroad, following his first vicharan in 1955.

One Way! Road Closed!

On the evening of 31 March 1960, Yogiji Maharaj set out for Broken Hill in Rajnibhai’s car. At one point along the journey, there was a diversion sign and the road had been blocked with bitumen drums. However, Rajnibhai got out of the car, moved them aside, and proceeded along that route.

Swamishri asked him, "Guru! Why did you get down?"
"Bapa! These people often keep the drums in place and the road closed even after repairs are complete. That is why I got down to move them," replied Rajnibhai.

Swamishri remarked, "That wouldn't be the case; they would only keep it closed if the road is indeed closed! We should take the car down the diversion."

However, Rajnibhai insisted, "Bapa! There won’t be any trouble. We should continue along this main road." Swamishri did not press the matter further.

After travelling about a mile, the car encountered a broken section of the road. It was now impossible to proceed. The road was narrow and elevated above the surrounding land, making it impossible to even turn the car around. Nor could the vehicle be driven off the road. They were forced to reverse the car.

Swamishri asked, "What's happened?"
"Bapa! We cannot go forward, and there is no room to turn the car back."
Swamishri burst into laughter and, raising one hand with a characteristic gesture of his finger, said, "One way! Road closed!"
He then added, "Likewise, for Akshardham, it is one-way! The roads are closed! One must never perceive flaws or shortcomings in others; one must only see their virtues. The path is closed for those who perceive flaws. Seeing virtues is the only way!"

It was somewhat late by the time they reached Broken Hill. They stayed at Lallubhai’s residence and held a sabha. Devotees and well-wishers from several villages in the Kheda region participated and benefited on that occasion.

He then added, "Likewise, for Akshardham, it is one-way! The roads are closed! One must never perceive flaws or shortcomings in others; one must only see their virtues. The path is closed for those who perceive flaws. Seeing virtues is the only way!"

It was somewhat late by the time they reached Broken Hill. They stayed at Lallubhai’s residence and held a sabha. Devotees and well-wishers from several villages in the Kheda region participated and benefited on that occasion.

(Yogiji Maharaj Jivan Chaitra Part 3/69)

6 February 2003
Maha sud 5
New Delhi, India

On the banks of the sacred River Yamuna, a prophecy was fulfilled. 

35 years earlier, Yogiji Maharaj had expressed his wish that a grand mandir dedicated to Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami be built in Delhi. 

On 6 February 2003, Pramukh Swami Maharaj realised this vision by inaugurating the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in New Delhi.

Crafted from Italian Carrara marble, the mandir was built in a record-breaking nine months through the tireless efforts of sadhus and volunteers.

Despite frail health and recovering from illness, Pramukh Swami Maharaj personally led the celebrations. From Mumbai, he encouraged sadhus to organise a grand festival, ensuring that Yogiji Maharaj’s wish be fulfilled with the highest standards of devotion and craftsmanship. 

With 250 sadhus and over 7,000 devotees from around the world in attendance, the murti-pratishtha ceremony took place on Vasant Panchmi, the auspicious birthday of Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj.

As part of a series of Yogi Jayanti celebrations at different locations across London in 1970, the fifth and final Yogi Jayanti was celebrated in Islington, London. 

Yogiji Maharaj is offered a cake by Prafulbhai on this occasion and grants divine bliss by cutting the cake and blowing the candles.

In tbis way, from 30 May to 3 June 1970, devotees celebrated the 78th birthday of Yogiji Maharaj at five different locations across London.

1. Durning Hall in Forest Gate, East London (Saturday 30 May)
2. Porchester Hall in Paddington, West London (Sunday 31 May)
3. Brent Town Hall in Wembley, North London (Monday 1 June)
4. Lambeth Town Hall in Brixton, South London (Tuesday 2 June)
5. Islington in Central London (Wednesday 3 June)

Barely 3 days had passed since Swamishri's 53rd birth celebrations in Ahmedabad.

In Vasad that morning, 15 padhramanis had been planned which started at 8.30am straight after puja on this day of a nirjala waterless fast.

By the time Swamishri returned to his utaaro that day at 3pm, he had visited 122 houses! 

Never one to rest on Ekadashi, Swamishri asked to lie down. His body felt warm. When Dr Swami measured Swamishri's temperature, it was 102°F!

It was then that he admitted he had been feeling feverish since morning.

After barely 30 minutes of rest, he continued his vicharan at 5.30pm.

Despite requests to take a little juice, he refused to break his fast, not even taking water. 
That evening he reached Sundalpura where he attended the night assembly until 11.45pm. By the time he lay down to sleep after cheshta, it was well past midnight.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj departed with nine sadhus amid a joyous farewell for his first Satsang tour abroad since his becoming guru in 1971. The plane took off from Mumbai at 10.15am and landed in Nairobi at 1.22pm. As the passengers disembarked, Pramukh Swami Maharaj and the sadhus were ordered to stay aboard. Then at 4.15pm, without any reason, they were instructed to fly back to Mumbai. Everyone in the group was saddened by the unexpected order to return. When a sadhu gave his diary to Swamishri during their flight back to Mumbai, he wrote, "The wish of Maharaj [Bhagwan Swaminarayan] and Bapa [Yogiji Maharaj] prevails. So, one should remain happy. Accept the ways they desire for you. Do not be pained or become miserable. Become aksharrup and offer devotion to God, then one will not be miserable."

At 2.45am Swamishri arrived in Mumbai. After reaching the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Dadar, he offered prostrations to the small murti of Thakorji, Shri Harikrishna Maharaj. Swamishri asked for his forgiveness in not being able to offer him food (thal) during their return journey to Mumbai. Swamishri had a fresh meal prepared at night and offered it to Thakorji while singing thal (devotional songs sung while offering food).

The following morning, Swamishri discoursed in a happy manner, inspiring laughter and joy in all the sadhus and devotees, thus making them forget the misery of him being sent back.

Watch full video documentary on this prasang: https://youtu.be/GF1kxIkrGPI

Murti Pratishtha at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, New York, USA

During Yogiji Maharaj’s visit to London in 1970, in which he consecrated the mandir in Islington, he gave ashirwad to Dr KC Patel that a mandir would soon be created in North America and that Pramukh Swami Maharaj would come for the pratishtha. 

True to his vision, in 1974, Pramukh Swami Maharaj embarked on his first overseas visit since becoming the guru of BAPS. 

During this historic visit, he consecrated this mandir in Flushing, New York with the installation of murtis previously consecrated in Jinja, Africa by Yogiji Maharaj in 1960. 

This was the very first BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in North America. 

Today, there are over 100 BAPS Mandirs in North America, including 6 traditional shikharbaddha mandirs.

On Saturday 30 July (Shravan Sud Poonam - Raksha Bandhan), Pramukh Swami Maharaj opened a new mandir in Wellingborough, the third BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir to be consecrated in a short span of 15 days.

The pictorial murtis of Akshar-Purushottam, Radha-Krishna and Guru Parampara were taken out in a grand procession through the streets of Wellingborough. 

Hundreds of devotees gathered to make history as the first Hindu Mandir in Wellingborough was opened at humble premises on Mill Road.

What began with a small group of devotees gathering together in 1972, and then a small Hari mandir on 16 Mill Road, has now, after the installation of the ‘Akshar Deri’ at the newly built mandir in 2009, become a pilgrimage centre for the UK devotees, and the venue for the annual Akhand Dhun.

Divine Revelation 

Soon after his hectic vicharan abroad of 1977-1978, Pramukh Swami Maharaj's health took a turn for the worse, and he was recuperating in Sarangpur due to this prolonged illness.

One evening, while resting in his room, Swamishri suddenly exclaimed, "Please call Narayan Bhagat immediately."

As soon as Narayan Bhagat [Pujya Viveksagar Swami] arrived, Swamishri signalled for all the other sadhus in the room to leave. Swamishri then, despite his grave illness, spoke in a low voice but clearly, "I see light... light... maybe this body will not remain..."

Hearing these words startled Narayan Bhagat. Before he could respond, Swamishri spoke again, "After me, place Mahant Swami as the guru."

In this way, Swamishri revealed his successor in the Gunatit Guru Parampara.

With time, Swamishri soon recovered, and a few months later, his vicharan continued unabated as before.

Prasang on Swamishri's devotion:
Following his cataract operation, Pramukh Swami was recovering in a room at the Massachusetts Eye and Ear Infirmary. His eyes were bandaged shut and so he called out and asked as to who was present. A local youth was sitting in the room and asked Swami what he needed. Since it was the evening, Swami asked him to recite the cheshta. The youth replied, “I don’t know the cheshta.” So Swami instructed him to read it from a kirtan book, which he did not have. At this point, Swami instructed the youth to open his own (Swami’s) puja, take out the ‘Nityavidhi’ and had him recite the cheshta from the book. Despite physical ailment, Swami’s desire to hear the cheshta did not waver.

The bicentenary birth celebrations of Bhagwan Swaminarayan were held in Ahmedabad as part of a 37-day festival from 7 March to 13 April 1981.

The 200th birth anniversary was celebrated on 12 April 1981. On this sunny morning, Pramukh Swami Maharaj initiated over 200 youths and parshads as renunciants. Not since Bhagwan Swaminarayan had initiated 500 paramhansas in one night in Kalvani had anyone in the Swaminarayan Sampradaya undertaken such a noble act - one that will forever be engraved in the memories of those fortunate enough to have witnessed this historic event.

📹 Video Smruti: https://youtu.be/VNL9i6yzbNA

---

Professor Raymond Williams, LaFollette Distinguished Professor in the Humanities emeritus and Professor of Religion (Chair) emeritus of Wabash College, writes:

"A major step in the removal of caste distinctions among ascetics was taken at the bicentenary celebrations of Swaminarayan’s birth, in April 1981, when 207 young men took initiation at Ahmedabad. Without prior announcement to the followers, Pramukh Swami took the occasion to give bhagvati diksha to approximately twenty ascetics from lower castes who had previously been permanently in white clothing. Castes such as blacksmiths and bargemen were represented. He performed the initiation ceremony for them, gave them new names and saffron clothing, and by that act abolished for BAPS the caste-related category of ascetics permanently in white. Henceforth, the period as bhagat has been temporary, only a preparation for final initiation as sadhu...The initiation produced great excitement among those present in Ahmedabad, and it was hailed as “a revolutionary act."

Chaitra Sud 6, VS 2007
Gadhada

To expound the pure principles of Akshar-Purushottam upasana as established by Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj created five shikharbaddha mandirs: Bochasan, Sarangpur, Gondal, Atladra and Gadhada.

On the auspicious land of Gadhada which had been blessed with the 25-year stay of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Shastriji Maharaj sought to acquire the land on the hill top on the banks of the sacred River Ghela. 

It was a colossal task, deemed impossible by many. Yet with faith in God and Guru, he persisted for 33 long years before finally acquiring the land in 1949.

Despite his advanced age and frail health, he meticulously oversaw the project of building a marble shikharbaddha mandir in Gadhada. 

During his final days in Sarangpur, despite being bedridden, he expressed a wish to travel to Gadhada. 

He travelled by car and reached Gadhada on the evening of 11 April 1951.

On the morning of 12 April 1951, he personally conducted the consecration of the murtis of Dham, Dhami and Mukta, bathing the murtis with sacred water from the River Ghela along with other pratishtha rituals.
After performing the arti, before preparing to return to Sarangpur, he exclaimed, "My vidhi is now over. Jogi Maharaj will come and complete the final consecration arti."

Six days following the passing of Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj performed the murti pratishtha of the murtis of Dham, Dhami and Mukta in the central shrine of the grand marble mandir on 16 May 1951.

Cholecystectomy operation performed on Pramukh Swami Maharaj at Cumballa Hill Hospital, Mumbai, by Dr A.R. Patel. His gall bladder was removed due to multiple gallstones.

Following the operation, Swamishri was resting in Gondal. One day, after Swamishri took breakfast, a balak named Chandrakant came rushing. He asked Swamishri in childish prattle, “Bapa, where is your operation scar?” He had once heard his parents talking about the operation.

The devotees who saw the child were quite surprised with the balak's request. Swamishri, however, lifted his upper cloth (gatariyu) and showed him the scar. He said to the balak, “Here, run your hand on it so that it heals soon.” Innocently, Chandrakant ran his hand on the scar.
Swamishri then remarked, “Now it will heal soon."

Such was Swamishri's affectionate nature.

Mumbai, India 

Cholecystectomy operation performed on Pramukh Swami Maharaj at Cumballa Hill Hospital, Mumbai, by Dr A.R. Patel. His gall bladder was removed due to multiple gallstones.

Following the operation, Swamishri was resting in Gondal. One day, after Swamishri took breakfast, a balak named Chandrakant came rushing. He asked Swamishri in childish prattle, “Bapa, where is your operation scar?” He had once heard his parents talking about the operation.

The devotees who saw the child were quite surprised with the balak's request. Swamishri, however, lifted his upper cloth (gatariyu) and showed him the scar. He said to the balak, “Here, run your hand on it so that it heals soon.” Innocently, Chandrakant ran his hand on the scar. Swamishri then remarked, “Now it will heal soon."

Such was Swamishri's affectionate nature.

It was past six in the morning in the village of Sundalpura near Anand. Pramukh Swami Maharaj had a jam packed programme ahead. Whilst bathing, he made no mention of the tightness in his chest, nor gave any physical clue. 

While attending to his morning routine, Swamishri was overcome with pain and sweating profusely. The sadhus rushed to him. He was suffering a heart attack at the age of 62. With no medical facilities available in the village, plans were soon made to transfer Swamishri to Dr. B.R. Patel's hospital in Vadodara, almost 50km away.

While Swamishri was being rushed to Vadodara in a high speed convoy of cars, his car suddenly screeched to a halt at a crossroad. Fearing the worst, everyone ran to Swamishri’s car. Swamishri appeared calm yet concerned. He called for Acharya Swami and told him, “Tomorrow, we were scheduled to attend the Shikshapatri parayan at Dahyabhai Gajjar’s place in Anand. Please go there and ensure that everything is taken care of. And explain why I won’t be able to come...” It is common medical knowledge that the first few hours after a heart attack are probably one of the most critical periods that any patient can ever face. 

Senior swamis, Mahant Swami and Dr Swami both cancelled their vicharan, and also rushed to Vadodara to ensure that Swamishri receive appropriate treatment. 

When Mahant Swami first saw Swamishri, he was hooked up to life support systems. In this state, Swamishri beckoned an attendant near and whispered, "Make sure you cook mag for Mahant Swami."

📹 Smruti Video: https://youtu.be/vGiQsMx5j7U

Despite this heart attack and setback, as soon as he had recovered and recuperated, Swamishri still continued his duties and vicharan, true to his promise to his guru Shastriji Maharaj. For 30 years, he continued to serve tirelessly day and night. 

For example, following eight months of hectic vicharan covering five continents in 1984, in a period of only six days in November 1984, Swamishri travelled to 22 villages to fulfill the sentiments of devotees. 

📹Photo-Story detailing this prasang: https://youtu.be/Ym4slDaEUUs

40 years ago today, Pramukh Swami Maharaj graced The Netherlands. He blessed the home of a devotee named Jeanette Groenen, a Dutch lady who made a wish on the bicentenary Swaminarayan Jayanti in 1981 that Pramukh Swami visit her home, which was fullfilled by Swamishri exactly three years later.

This video above is her memory of this magical surprise, which fell on the auspicious day of Swaminarayan Jayanti & Rama Navami. 

See unique historical footage and hear this prasang narrated by eyewitnesses Pujya Viveksagar Swami, Pujya Vivekjivan Swami, and Han Kop here:
https://youtu.be/kz7bzzpNwAI?t=2408 (link will automatically open at the appropriate time)

---

11 April 1911 
Chaitra sud 13, VS 1967
Bhagvati Diksha of Yogiji Maharaj in Vartal

Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj was born as Jhinabhai in the village of Dhari on 23 May 1892. 

His childhood was one of devotion par excellence along with samagam of the visiting sadhus from the Swaminarayan Mandir in Junagadh, including Sadguru Krishnacharan Swami.

It was under the guidance of Krishnacharan Swami that young Jhinabhai renounced home at the tender age of 16 with the blessings of his family. He joined the order of parshads in Junagadh in November 1908.

In Junagadh, young Jhina Bhagat served in various capacities as a parshad, winning the affection of the sadhus and devotees.

On the morning of 11 April 1911, 18-year-old Jhina Bhagat took bhagvati diksha into saffron at the hands of Acharya Shripatiprasadji Maharaj in Vartal.

On this auspicious occasion, Jhina Bhagat was renamed Sadhu Gnanjivandasji.

Due to his austere and devout nature, the sadhus and devotees fondly called him ‘Yogi’ or 'Jogi' while Krishnacharandas Swami called him ‘Gnanji Swami’.

He served as a sadhu in Junagadh Mandir for three months before taking a decision that turned out to be a pivotal development in the history of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha.

During the vicharan, the devotees took Swamishri to bless several iconic locations as well as bless the homes of local devotees.
